posts.title: Framing Isolation: Wide Lenses in the Spaghetti Western
posts.summary: Notes on how Sergio Leone and Tonino Delli Colli used extreme wide-angle lenses juxtaposed against tight eye-level close-ups to build tension before a single line of dialogue is spoken.
posts.body:
Watching Once Upon a Time in the West again with the sound turned off reveals how much of the narrative architecture sits purely in lens choice and blocking. Rather than cutting back and forth in standard over-the-shoulder coverage, Leone holds the frame until the environment itself becomes an antagonist.

For my upcoming short, I am testing a 24mm prime at low angles to exaggerate foreground geometry while keeping background movement sparse.

posts.title: Drafting Scene 4: Pacing Dialogue Without Exposition
posts.summary: Rewriting the diner confrontation to strip out subtext spoken aloud, letting physical action and silence carry the scene's turning point.
posts.body: First drafts always suffer from characters explaining how they feel. In the second pass of the script, I cut forty percent of the spoken lines and replaced them with beats of stillness—a coffee cup pushed across laminate, a glance toward the exit.
